newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Dec farm import value down 4.3 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Dec farm import value down 4.3 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The value of Taiwan's agriculture imports in December was US$219.7 million, down 4.3 percent from US$229.5 million in December 1995, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
For all of 1996, agriculture imports totalled US$3.1649 billion, up 20.7 percent from US$2.6223 billion in 1995, the ministry said in a statement.
Grain and oilseed imports were the top agriculture import items both in December and for the full year.
Taiwan traders said the reduced import value in December reflected lower world grain and oilseed prices during the period, rather than a downturn in imports.

They attributed the year-on-year rise to the same phenomenon in reverse, noting that world grain and oilseed prices peaked at record levels in mid-1996, resulting in higher average monthly import values during much of the year.
Actual December import tonnages were not available, but traders estimated 380,000 tonnes of corn and 140,000 tonnes of soybean would have arrived at Taiwan ports in the month.

Official import tonnages for all of 1996 also were not disclosed but local traders estimated the totals at 6.5 million tonnes of corn and 2.4 million tonnes of soybeans, virtually all of it sourced in the United States.
